inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E = midpoint of the raised Q3 FY26 guidance ($12.1-12.2B). FY2026 ends 2026-10-25 with three quarters reported (9M FY26 revenue $8,961m vs $8,921m 9M FY25), so the guidance year is FY0 and the growth path starts at FY2027.
inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average shares, Q3 FY2026 10-Q (quarter ended 2026-07-26): 551.074m vs 550.675m basic. Held FLAT: SBC (~$26m/yr, 0.21% of revenue) is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would double-charge it. No buybacks FY2024-FY2026 (financing outflow $0), so the flat count is a modelling convention, not a funded one -- the ~0.1%/yr creep from grants is immaterial.
inputs.net_debt_note: Q3 FY2026 balance sheet (2026-07-26): current LTD $505.6m + non-current LTD $2,349.5m = $2,855.1m; cash $839.6m. Operating lease liabilities ($168m at FY25) EXCLUDED -- lease cost is expensed inside EBITDA under US GAAP (treatment B).
inputs.reported_fcf_note: TTM to Q3 FY2026: FY2025 $534.3m + 9M FY26 $549.4m - 9M FY25 $302.9m = $780.8m (OCF less capex). FY2025 alone was $534.3m (working-capital build) and FY2024 $1,010.3m (working-capital release); the TTM sits between them.
inputs.sbc_source: Cash-flow-statement share-based compensation add-back, SEC XBRL (ShareBasedCompensation): FY2025 $25.6m, FY2024 $23.2m, H1 FY26 $16.4m; TTM approximated at $26.0m. Hormel publishes no combined SBC-plus-withholding figure and PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation is not tagged; withholding is immaterial at this grant size.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: Hormel is a net-debt company (net debt $2.0B vs owner FCF ~$0.75B), so the rule 'deduct interest income when net cash > 1x FCF' does not apply. Interest/investment income is not separately tagged in XBRL; it is not inside EBITDA-built flows either.
inputs.dividends_note: Dividends $633m FY2025 ($1.16/sh), $1.17/sh FY2026 run-rate -- roughly 85% of owner FCF. Not a model input (unlevered DCF) but explains why no buybacks fund the flat count.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: Last Sunday of October (52/53-week; FY2026 ends 2026-10-25)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Bottom-up: 10y UST ~4.2%, beta 0.55 (packaged-food staple), ERP 5.0% -> cost of equity ~7.0%; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.5% (legacy 1.7-3.05% notes refinancing higher; $500m matures FY2027), after-tax ~3.5%; weights ~80% equity ($11.0B market cap) / 20% debt ($2.86B) -> ~6.3%. Used 7.0%, the folder's floor for an operating company, applied identically to all three scenarios. Commodity cyclicality, guidance-credibility and CEO-transition risk are charged ONCE, in the scenario paths and the 25% bear weight, not as a WACC premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: B (leases as operating cost). US GAAP operating lease expense is already inside operating income/EBITDA; operating lease liabilities ($168.0m at FY2025) are excluded from net debt. Finance leases immaterial. D&A used for the tax build is the reported DepreciationDepletionAndAmortization line ($263.9m FY25), which excludes operating ROU amortisation, so the lease is not charged twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interest $16.2m (Q3 FY26) deducted once in the equity bridge; flows are consolidated. Attributable NI ties to consolidated NI within $1m.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component-built (SKILL.md row: operating company, consumer/cyclical -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. MID-CYCLE NORMALISATION: FY2025 GAAP (op margin 5.9%, NI $478m, EPS $0.87) and Q3 FY26 (op margin 3.7%, EPS $0.11) both carry non-repeating charges -- a $105.8m equity-method impairment in FY2025 and a further $37.1m equity-method loss plus operating-level charges in Q3 FY26 (restructuring tagged at only $8.5m 9M FY26, so the rest is impairment/legal-type items not itemised in XBRL). The forward EBITDA margin path therefore anchors to the ADJUSTED FY2026 run-rate implied by guidance (adj EPS $1.45-1.51 = +6-10% on FY25 adj ~$1.37; adj operating income ~$940m, ~7.7%; adj EBITDA ~$1.21B, ~10.0% of $12.15B), NOT to the FY2025 GAAP trough, and ramps toward the FY2022-24 adjusted mid-cycle of ~11.3-12.4% -- the same treatment as SAN.NZ / BSL.AX / HAL (mid-cycle owner-FCF). Equity-method earnings (MegaMex etc., ~$45-55m/yr in normal years) are OUTSIDE the EBITDA-built flows, so the $527.9m affiliate stake is added to the bridge at book (matching-asset rule); pension non-service income and rabbi-trust investment income are likewise excluded from the flows with no asset added (conservative). Working capital: receivables + inventory > payables (~13% of revenue), so growth consumes cash: wc_capture -12%. Terminal cap 16x FCF on base binds over Gordon (20.4x at 7%/2%): a 6.25% FCF yield for a 2%-growth staple. Dividend payout ~85% of owner FCF leaves no buyback capacity; count held flat because grants are tiny, not because they are repurchased.

equity_bridge.item: Investments in affiliates (equity-method stakes, MegaMex etc.) at book
equity_bridge.note: Q3 FY2026 10-Q balance sheet, InvestmentsInAffiliatesSubsidiariesAssociatesAndJointVentures $527.864m. Equity earnings excluded from EBITDA flows, so the asset is added once. Book is post the FY2025 $105.8m impairment; normal-year equity earnings of ~$50m would capitalise higher.
Q3 FY2026 MinorityInterest $16.210m; consolidated flows, so deducted once here.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: FY2025 organic growth ~2%, FY2026 guidance $12.1-12.2B (+0.5% incl. portfolio-shaping exits), US packaged-food volume growth low-single-digit; equity CAGR (4.2%) is inflated by retained earnings on a shrinking-earnings base and revenue 5yr CAGR (4.7%) by the June-2021 Planters acquisition ($3.35B, FY2021 revenue +18.5%)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR +4.2% vs EPS 5yr -12.4% and owner-FCF 5yr -7.2%: divergence far beyond 30%. Book value compounds only because ~$640m of dividends is less than reported profit; the earnings and cash-flow series say the business shrank. Neither series is a usable forward anchor -- revenue base FY2020-25 includes Planters, EPS/FCF FY2025 endpoints carry ~$275m after-tax of non-repeating charges.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs FY2020->FY2025 (5yr) and FY2022->FY2025 (3yr), owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC (interest income 0): FY2020 $738.0m, FY2022 $831.1m, FY2025 $508.7m. Owner-FCF CAGRs (-7.2% / -15.1%) are only ~0.5pp below reported (-6.8% / -14.5%): SBC is flat at ~$23-26m, so stock is not paying for growth here -- the decline is real cash-flow erosion from protein input inflation, the FY2025 working-capital build, and capex stepping up to $311m.

base.ebitda_margin_rationale: FY27 10.2% is a small step from the ~10.0% adjusted FY26 run-rate implied by guidance; recovers to 11.5% by FY31 = the FY2023-24 adjusted level (11.3%) plus part of the T&M savings, but below FY2022's 12.4% and well below the pre-Planters FY2016-19 14-15%, which the turkey-heavy mix and beef/pork cost structure no longer support.
base.tax_rationale: 22.5%: FY2022-24 effective 21.5-22.5%; FY25 28% and 9M FY26 26.7% are inflated by non-deductible affiliate impairments.

scenario_narratives.base: Hormel is a mature branded-protein company whose FY2025 and Q3 FY26 GAAP numbers are a trough, not a run-rate. Revenue grows 2-2.5% (branded foodservice, Applegate and Jennie-O ground turkey offsetting the deliberate exits from whole-bird turkey, private-label nuts and contract manufacturing), and adjusted EBITDA margin climbs from the ~10% guided FY26 level to 11.5% by FY31 as pork costs moderate from the FY25 peak, avian-flu turkey supply normalises after 1H FY26, and Transform & Modernize plus the November-2025 corporate restructuring (~250 roles) deliver structural savings. It does NOT assume a return to the FY2016-19 14-15% margins: the Planters/Jennie-O mix, elevated beef costs and private-label pressure cap the recovery at roughly the FY2022-24 adjusted range. Terminal value at 16x owner FCF (cap binds over Gordon).
scenario_narratives.bull: Incoming CEO John Ghingo (Mondelez/Planters brand-builder, from 2026-10-26) executes a brand-led plan: innovation and marketing lift Retail mix, foodservice premium prepared proteins keep compounding, the International/China JV drag is fixed or exited, and T&M savings flow to margin rather than being reinvested against commodity inflation. Revenue grows 3-3.5% in the early years and adjusted EBITDA margin reaches 13% by FY32 -- a full recovery to FY2022 and beyond, though still short of the pre-Planters peak. The re-rating from a 13x forward P/E toward the staples-peer high-teens is captured by the 18x terminal cap and 2.5% terminal growth.
scenario_narratives.bear: The three-CEO transition in 18 months does not fix a structurally weaker portfolio: another avian-flu or ASF shock hits Jennie-O/pork in FY27-28, beef costs stay elevated, private-label trade-down continues in center-of-store, and the guidance-reset pattern of 2023-2025 repeats. Revenue barely grows (0.5-1.5%) and adjusted EBITDA margin never recovers past ~9.8% -- the FY26 guided level minus another cost cycle. The ~85% dividend payout leaves no capacity to buy back stock or de-lever meaningfully, so the market keeps applying a commodity-processor multiple: 13x terminal cap and 1.5% terminal growth.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: three guidance resets in 2023-2025, a $106m affiliate impairment in FY25 and a further Q3 FY26 charge, structurally exposed turkey vertical integration and a three-CEO transition make a no-recovery path a genuine possibility rather than a tail. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs T&M savings, commodity relief AND a new CEO's brand plan all to land together. Base 50%: the raised and narrowed FY26 guidance is evidence the trough is behind, but not that the FY2022 margin returns.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Hormel as a mid-cycle owner-FCF stream, not at the FY2025/Q3 FY26 GAAP trough and not at the FY2016-19 peak. The margin is component-built each year from the adjusted FY26 run-rate that guidance implies; charges that will not repeat (affiliate impairments, restructuring, Q3 FY26 items) are excluded from the anchor but their recurrence is priced through a 25% bear weight and a 13x bear terminal cap. Risk is charged once -- in the scenario flows and weights -- with one 7% USD WACC across scenarios. Equity-method affiliates are outside the flows and added at book; leases are inside EBITDA and outside net debt; SBC is expensed and the count held flat.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin anchor: the FY26 adjusted EBITDA (~10%) is inferred from guided adjusted EPS/operating-income growth, not a reported adjusted EBITDA line; if FY25 adjusted EPS was lower than the ~$1.37 implied by '6-10% growth to $1.45-1.51', the whole path shifts down
Terminal value is ~55-60% of EV and the 16x cap binds; at a 14x cap base IV falls roughly $2/share
Working-capital swings (FY24 +$0.5B release, FY25 build) make any single-year FCF a poor anchor; the TTM $781m reported FCF sits mid-range but is not guaranteed
Commodity shocks (avian flu, ASF, beef) can take 200-300bp off margin for 1-2 years at a time, as FY2023-25 showed
$505m of notes mature in FY2027 and refinance at ~4.5-5% vs 1.7-3.05% coupons: ~$15-20m/yr of extra interest (outside the unlevered flows, but relevant to EPS and the dividend cover)
Dividend at ~85% of owner FCF: any further FCF decline forces a payout-ratio breach or debt-funded dividends
